✗ Ingress/api is unhealthy

ROOT CAUSE
  Container "api" is failing its readiness probe (2 of 2 Pods)

  A container that fails its readiness probe is removed from the endpoints of
  every Service that selects this Pod, so it receives no traffic. Kubernetes
  reports that the probe failed; the reason the application answered that way is
  in its own logs.

  Evidence
    reason                 Unhealthy
      Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
    readinessProbe         http GET /healthz on port 8080
    readinessProbe.timing  delay 5s, period 10s, timeout 1s, failureThreshold 3
    lastSeen               1m ago

  Possible causes
    • the application is not listening on the probed port or path yet
    • the application takes longer to answer than the probe allows
    • the probe points at a port or path the application does not serve

  Suggested action
    Compare the probe's target with what the application actually serves, and
    check the container's logs around the failures.
      kubectl logs api-abc -n prod -c api

ALSO DETECTED
  Service "admin" does not exist, so its routes lead nowhere

  The Ingress routes to Service "admin", and the API server reports that no such
  Service exists in namespace "prod". A controller cannot build a backend for
  it.

  Evidence
    route          api.example.com/admin -> Service/admin:80
    service/admin  NotFound

  Possible causes
    • the Service was renamed or deleted
    • the Ingress and the Service are in different namespaces, which an Ingress
      cannot cross

  Suggested action
    Create the Service, or correct the backend name in the Ingress.
      kubectl get services -n prod

CONSEQUENCE
  Service "api" has no ready endpoints, so its routes return errors

  The Ingress and the Service are configured correctly, but the Service
  currently routes to nothing. Requests that reach these routes have no backend
  to be served by.

  Evidence
    route              api.example.com/ -> Service/api:80
    readyEndpoints     0
    notReadyEndpoints  2
    matchingPods       2

  Suggested action
    Ask KubeWhy about the Service itself for the full endpoint picture.
      kubectl why service api -n prod

Ingress
  Class    nginx  exists
  Address  lb.example.com

Routes
  api.example.com/       Service/api:80    0 of 2 endpoints ready
  api.example.com/admin  Service/admin:80  Service not found
